prompt:
I need the front end for Reelhouse. A shared project home for small documentary production companies that holds every reel, scene, clip, interview transcript and archival clearance for each film the team is making.

Who's using it: Ama Boateng, an assistant editor who joined a 9-person documentary company two weeks ago. She's skilled in editing software but still learning how this team organizes its projects and where things live.

What they're doing right now: The director has asked her to confirm that the 1970s news footage used in Reel 3, Scene 22 of the feature "Salt Road" has been cleared for festival use, then pull the interview passage that plays right after it. A colleague's message only said "it's under the Hartwell archive stuff somewhere." She needs to figure out which project and reel she's currently in, get to the scene, follow it to the archival item and its clearance record, and then reach the right interview transcript without losing her way back.

What's in the system at this point: The company has 3 active projects: "Salt Road" (feature, in fine cut), "Night Ferry" (6-part series, in assembly) and a short for a commissioning broadcaster. "Salt Road" has 6 reels, 84 scenes, about 1,900 clips, 212 archival items from 7 sources (Hartwell Newsfilm Library supplies 61 of them), and 41 interview transcripts. Clearance statuses are cleared-all-media, cleared-festival-only, pending and denied. Scene 22 uses Hartwell item HNL-1974-0317, which is pending, with the request sent Oct 28. The next scene uses an interview with retired dockworker Leonard Pike, timecode 01:12:40–01:14:05. Ama has 6 recently visited items and 2 saved shortcuts.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
